Local leaders share their thoughts on the eve of the nation's 250th anniversary by PQ Staff 2026 Summer July 29, 2026 On the eve of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, we asked a group of leading Pittsburghers to consider and answer that question. We thank them for giving their thoughts on this important occasion. MARK WIEDMAN, PRESIDENT, PNC America represents the promise that where you start doesn’t have to define where you end. It’s a country built on reinvention, where each generation moves us closer to our ideals. Pittsburgh reflects that spirit. Once forged by steel and industrial grit, it helped build the backbone of the nation. Today, as a center of innovation, technology, and healthcare, it’s shaping what comes next. Different eras, same purpose: pushing America forward. America is opportunity, resilience, and the confidence that tomorrow can be better than today. MAGGIE HARDY, OWNER & CEO, 84 LUMBER To me, having grown up in western Pennsylvania with my father, who started 84 Lumber 70 years ago, America means opportunity. Being privately held, we have the opportunity to make a difference for each person we touch in our company, through our customers, associates, vendors, and partners. For example, during Hurricane Katrina (just one of many natural disasters), we were the first boots on the ground to offer support. As America approaches its 250th year, it is our mission to deliver the American Dream to our people, watch them grow, and become future leaders that drive America for the next 250 years. TAO HE, BOARD DIRECTOR, PITTSBURGH CHINESE CULTURE CENTER As a Chinese immigrant who has lived in Pittsburgh for more than 20 years, America still means opportunities that I never would have had while in China. In China, I was a janitor working at a hotel. In the U.S., I am a CPA working at an over-100-year-old accounting firm. America means faith, which I found in Pittsburgh, and this helped me find my identity and my purpose in life. America means another chance, that I can push the restart button after each failure. I can learn and grow from my failures. America means family, which I am building up with my wife and my beautiful son and daughter. America means that I can forever dream big, work hard and have another chance. Thank you for everything, America. Happy 250th birthday, America. Long live America! JEFF FINKELSTEIN, PRESIDENT & CEO, JEWISH FEDERATION OF PITTSBURGH For my family, America wasn’t just opportunity; it was survival. All four of my grandparents came to America from Europe in the early 1900s. One, my grandfather Irving, arrived alone in Boston at age 20 with little education and nothing promised. He learned a trade, worked with dignity into his 70s, and built a life rooted in freedom and opportunity. While his family members who remained in Latvia were murdered by the Nazis, his descendants were given a future here. Their survival is America’s promise. I still believe in that promise — as a proud American, and a proud American Jew. KANAK IYER, FOUNDING PRESIDENT, ASIAN AMERICAN CHAMBER OF COMMERCE PITTSBURGH The American Dream is why so many of us come here. Did I achieve it? Not in conventional terms. But I have lived life on my own terms — the freedom to pursue a scientific dream. Could I have done that in India? Not at that time; the resources didn’t exist. In America, as a 27-year-old immigrant, I had my “aha” moment in a remarkable laboratory, an opportunity for which I will always be grateful. What followed were challenges: learning how to navigate the system and confronting systemic barriers. Yet none of that stopped me. I became an entrepreneur before I even knew the word, built my own enterprise, and found my way back to science to pursue what once felt impossible. That is what America means to me: possibility, resilience, and opportunity. REV. PAUL T. ABERNATHY, CEO, NEIGHBORHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT America is, above all, an idea by which people of goodwill continually form a political union founded on values expressed through radical commitment to honor the God-given dignity of all persons. As Americans, we speak of this union not in the sense of land, ethnicity, language or religion, but rather, as laws that guarantee the free pursuit of beauty, truth and goodness for every human within our borders. As we celebrate the 250th anniversary of this nation, I pray that it is the idea of America far more than the history of America that guides us well into our future. DAN ONORATO, EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT, HIGHMARK HEALTH & FORMER ALLEGHENY COUNTY EXECUTIVE America is both a promise and a responsibility. It is the promise that where you start doesn’t limit where you can go. Growing up on the North Side of Pittsburgh, I saw how hard work, strong communities, and opportunity can change lives and revive places. America also represents a responsibility to serve others and build institutions that endure. In public service, I’ve learned that responsibility is all about listening, solving real problems, and caring for people when they’re most vulnerable. At 250 years, we continue to shape the promise of this great nation and bear the responsibility of making it better today and tomorrow than it was yesterday. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/14/farag.text: British politician Nigel Farage has comfortably won a local by-election on Friday after all the main political parties boycotted the vote in protest.The former MEP had declared a "resounding victory" early Friday but said he would not attend the official result announcement that pitted him against Count Binface and a list of independent candidates.Farage picked up over 22,000 votes in an election that saw a 44% turnout."The verdict is in and it is a convincing and overwhelming win," he said as supporters chanted his name at an event in Essex, which was broadcast on X.Farage triggered the vote by resigning his parliamentary seat, which he had held since 2024, over an investigation into his finances in the constituency of Clacton in the county of Essex.The vote had been shunned by Britain's main political parties, including the ruling Labour Party, as a stunt by the Reform UK leader - once touted as a potential prime minister - to dodge scrutiny of his dealings.That has left candidates such as Binface - the alter ego of comedian Jon Harvey - to seize the spotlight."What an upside-down world it is, where Count Binface is now the candidate of the establishment," Farage said in his speech.He said he would not attend the count, where candidates traditionally gather for the declaration of results, saying Essex Police had warned him that an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result" was planned.The BBC reported that this was not true, quoting Essex Police in a statement that read: "We have a proportionate and robust policing operation to ensure the safety and security of all participants in the count."Acting Returning Officer Ian Davidson said election officials had worked with police to ensure the process was "completed safely and securely", adding there was "no reason not to proceed with the count process at this time".Analysts expected a win for Farage, but forecast that the self-styled "intergalactic space warrior", who campaigns wearing a rubbish bin on his head, could secure an uncomfortably large share of the vote, possibly approaching 20 percent.Binface took to social media after the result to declare himself the winner "of the candidates that 'bothered to turn up for the results'" and, in a video, suggested Farage had been "humiliated" as one in four people in Clacton would prefer him to the Reform UK leader.Turnout reached about 44.7 percent, down from 59 percent in the 2024 general election.In the coastal community, many voters appeared unenthusiastic about the poll, with even some Reform party volunteers describing the contest as a joke."It's a bit ridiculous," party campaigner Jane Embelton told AFP."It's all to make Nigel Farage look like an idiot, basically. But he doesn't look like an idiot to me or his supporters."A record 33 fringe candidates, including Binface, stood in the vote, with some of the longest ballot papers in the country's history seen being unfolded at Clacton Leisure Centre, where the count was held.- 'We can't decide' -Farage, whose party had topped national polls for 18 months before falling behind recently, surprised voters with his July 7 resignation amid the probe into his finances.The investigation by the parliamentary sleaze watchdog is examining allegations he and Reform's deputy leader, Richard Tice, failed to declare financial gifts. They deny any wrongdoing.Farage has framed Thursday's vote as "the people of Clacton versus the Establishment", aimed at thwarting the "stitch-up" over his finances."The people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions," he said in a video released before casting his vote.Clacton voter Phil predicted the vote was "not going to change anything", noting if Farage won as expected, the parliamentary probe would restart.Political pundits have downplayed the vote's wider significance in a constituency that overwhelmingly backed Brexit a decade ago."It will be astonishing if Farage were not to win," political scientist John Curtice told AFP.But some assessed Farage's election gambit had backfired as his Reform party slips down national polls."Farage's plan to turn this by-election into a serious political battle failed," Queen Mary University of London politics professor Stijn van Kessel told AFP, noting the resulting spectacle "makes Farage look rather silly".Farage netted 46 percent of the vote in the 2024 general election to become an MP on his eighth attempt.- Police probe -The probe into Farage, which paused when he resigned, relates to a £5 million ($6.7m) donation from cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.Meanwhile, London police have confirmed starting a investigation last year into donations to Reform before the 2024 election.UK media have reported that the police probe concerns undeclared financial support from longtime Farage ally and convicted fraudster George Cottrell and his mother.The decision to trigger a by-election has seen a drop in support for Reform, which recently won a vast number of council elections across the UK in May.

https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/08/15/d.text: Menü Kereső Példátlan drónhullám volt Románia határánál, 96 óra alatt több mint száz eszközt észleltek a radarok Transtelex Legfontosabb frissítve Vig Emese (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Az elmúlt négy napban nem győzték kihalászni, összeszedni, megsemmisíteni a Románia területére esett dróndarabokat a folyamatos készenlétben álló katonai intervenciós csapatok. A védelmi miniszter számokat is közölt és néhány fotó kíséretében megosztotta a Facebook oldalán: mindössze 96 óra leforgása alatt a román hadsereg radarjai több mint száz drónt észleltek az ország légterének közelében, közölte Radu Miruță. A miniszter szerint ez azért van, mert példátlan intenzitásúvá váltak az orosz támadások a román határ közvetlen szomszédságában. A pilóta nélküli drónok rajokban támadták a Duna-parti ukrán kikötőket, és bár többségüket az ukrán légvédelem megsemmisítette, a roncsok és lezuhanó eszközökből most már egyre több került át a román határon. A hadsereg a drónok miatt az elmúlt napokban kilencszer emelte a légvédelmi készültséget, a NATO harci repülőgépei pedig hét alkalommal szálltak fel járőrözni vagy felderíteni, hogy mi történik. Három esetben katonai helikoptereket is bevetettek. A következmények pénteken a Duna-deltában és a tengerparton is megmutatkoztak. Tulcea megyében két külön helyszínen is lezuhant drónokat azonosítottak: Plauru térségében és Luncavița környékén bukkantak roncsokra, ahol az alacsonyan szálló drón, amit a radarok nem is érzékeltek, amikor becsapódott, robbanást és tüzet is okozott az erdős területen. Ezzel párhuzamosan a tengerparti üdülőhelyekre is kisodorták a hullámok a háborús hordalékot. Costinești-en egymás után két napon is dróndarabok miatt kellett kordonok mögé zárni a strandot, ami miatt a fürdőzéstől eltiltott turisták elkezdtek kiabálni a biztonsági intézkedéseket felügyelő csendőrökre . Péntek délután aztán Saturn strandjának egy részét is kiürítették a hatóságok, miután ott is drónburkolatot találtak a homokban, a katonák a tengerből próbálták kihalászni az alkatrészeket. Augusztus 15-e egyébként éppen a román haditengerészet napja, és az ünnepségeket a tengerparti Konstancán rendezték meg , ahol a politikai vezetés szinte kivétel nélkül arról beszélt, mekkora stratégiai jelentőséggel bír a Fekete-tenger térségének biztonsága. Románia több mint 5,6 milliárd euró értékű katonai beszerzési szerződést írt alá az Európai Unió SAFE programjában. A védelmi minisztérium ebből 981,95 millió euróért korszerű drónelhárító és légvédelmi rendszereket vásárol a Rheinmetalltól. Kapcsolódó Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://oilprice.com/Energy/Energy-Gener.text: Azerbaijan is one of the world's oldest oil producers and exporters, having pumped crude since the mid-19th century, and remains a major global oil producer. It has long relied on oil and gas to meet its energy needs and as a major economic contributor. However, the host of the 29th UN Climate Change Conference COP29 in 2024 is now looking to diversify its energy mix by deploying more renewable energy capacity. Natural gas contributed 67 per cent of Azerbaijan's energy supply in 2023, while oil and oil products accounted for 31.1% and hydropower and other renewable energy sources contributed less than 2 per cent of the energy mix. Despite its longstanding reliance on oil and gas hydrocarbons still account for almost half of Azerbaijan's GDP the government has major plans to expand its renewable energy capacity to support greater diversification and strengthen energy security. In March 2025, the World Bank approved the Azerbaijan Scaling-Up Renewable Energy Project AZURE, which aims to strengthen Azerbaijan's power transmission network, support energy diversification, and meet the country's growing energy demand. The $173.5 million loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development IBRD is expected to help expand and modernise Azerbaijan's energy infrastructure and encourage private investment in its renewable energy sector, particularly in onshore wind. The initiative, which is part of the World Bank's Europe and Central Asia Renewable Energy Scale-up ECARES multi-year programme, is expected to help attract an initial $384 million in private investments. In November 2025, the government updated its national climate action plan to include ambitious renewable energy targets. Azerbaijan now aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 40 per cent, from 1990 levels. It also aims to boost the share of energy that comes from renewables to 30 per cent by 2030. Significant progress in renewable energy expansion in recent years means that Azerbaijan may surpass this target, generating up to 38 per cent of its power from clean sources. The government has introduced favourable policies in recent years to encourage greater investment in renewable energy development, including tax breaks for projects valued at up to $17.7 million and for renewable energy facilities with installed capacity of over 100 MW. This has already helped the country to attract investors, with the commissioning of the 240-megawatt Khizi-Absheron Wind Farm in January 2026 and the approval of the Garadagh Solar Power Plant in the Caspian region in 2023, which generates enough electricity to power 110,000 homes. The government is also focusing on developing "green energy corridors", including plans for a high-voltage transmission line, which will run under the Black Sea and into Georgia. The development of these routes is expected to help Azerbaijan become a major renewable energy exporter to Central Asia and Europe, thereby diversifying energy trade routes in the region. Amin Mammadov, Deputy Chairman of the Public Council under the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, explained, "Azerbaijan has been an energy hub for a very long time We want to also do that for green energy." The three main routes of focus are the Caspian-Black Sea-Europe Corridor, the Azerbaijan-Trkiye-Europe Corridor, and the Central Asia-Azerbaijan-Europe Corridor. Together, the three corridors are expected to be capable of transporting 10 GW of renewable electricity once complete. In 2022, Azerbaijan signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement on Green Energy Development and Transmission with Georgia, Romania, and Hungary, supporting the development of a green energy corridor to Europe. In July, Azerbaijan announced major plans for offshore wind by designating 711.4 km2 of Caspian Sea waters as a renewable energy zone for offshore wind development. This followed a recent agreement between Azerbaijan's Energy Ministry and Clean Energy Capital, a subsidiary of Azerbaijan Green Energy Company, for the firm to conduct research on an offshore wind project in a designated area of the Caspian Sea. In June 2025, Azerbaijan's Energy Ministry also signed a deal with China Energy Engineering Corporation to explore the development of a 200 MW offshore wind project. The Ministry had signed two other agreements with Chinese firms for offshore wind development earlier that year. Azerbaijan also signed agreements with BP to develop a $200 million, 240 MW solar power plant in Karabakh in June 2025, which BP aims to complete by mid-2027. Meanwhile, ACWA Power's 240 MW Khizi-Absheron Wind Farm, the country's first large-scale, independently developed wind project, became fully operational last year. It is expected to provide clean power to over 300,000 Azerbaijani households. While Azerbaijan intends to continue producing oil and gas, the government also has major plans for the country's renewable energy sector. Expanding its clean energy capacity by developing wind, solar, hydropower, and battery storage projects will help diversify the electricity mix and enhance energy security. Meanwhile, the creation of green corridors connecting Asia and Europe will help establish Azerbaijan as a clean energy and trade hub. By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com
